blocks.text: Leviticus 7 completes regulations for the guilt and peace offerings and distinguishes thank offerings from vows and freewill offerings. It sets time limits for eating sacrificial flesh, prohibits eating fat and blood, and identifies the portions assigned to priests. Supplied contextual evidence for this passage adds: Ancient Near Eastern ritual comparisons illuminate vocabulary and practice but do not establish that Israelite rites carried the same theology or were directly borrowed.
